docs.title: cnv-sc-rs
docs.text:
Copy number inference from single cell expression, in Rust, with a thin Python layer on top.

It is a port of the expression path of numbat (Gao et al., Nature Biotechnology 2023) and its numerics package hahmmr, both MIT:

  1. A smoothed log-ratio signal per cell against a set of normal reference cells, binned along the genome (the inferCNV view).
  2. A cell hierarchy on that signal, cut into pseudobulks.
  3. A Poisson-lognormal HMM per pseudobulk, then consensus segments across pseudobulks, retested for a gain, loss or LOH call.
  4. Per-cell posteriors for every non-neutral segment and a tree-free tumour probability per cell.

No allele data and no clone phylogeny yet; those are later tiers of the Rust crate.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install cnv-sc-rs              # numpy, scipy, polars
pip install "cnv-sc-rs[anndata]"   # plus infer_cnv_adata

Wheels are abi3, so one wheel covers Python 3.10 onwards.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Raw UMI counts, cells x genes, as a scipy sparse matrix. Not normalised, not log-transformed.
  • Gene loci: chromosome, start and end per gene, on the genome build your annotation uses. Genes off chromosomes 1 to 22 are dropped, as in numbat.
  • Normal reference cells: cells you are confident carry no CNV, for instance immune or stromal cells from the same sample. Several cell types? Label them and each gets its own profile.

Start with the quickstart, or go to the scanpy guide if your data lives in an AnnData.

docs.title: infer_cnv
docs.text:
infer_cnv(
    X: SparseMatrix,
    chrom: ArrayLike,
    start: ArrayLike,
    end: ArrayLike,
    reference: ArrayLike,
    *,
    reference_labels: ArrayLike | None = None,
    params: CnvParams | None = None,
    genome: Genome = "hg38",
    n_threads: int | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> CnvResult

Copy number inference from single cell expression.

The expression path of numbat: smoothed log-ratio signal against the reference cells, a cell hierarchy, Poisson-lognormal HMMs on pseudobulks, consensus segments, then per-cell segment posteriors and a tumour/normal call per cell.

Genes off chromosomes 1 to 22, or with missing coordinates, are dropped.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default X SparseMatrix

Cells x genes raw UMI counts, any scipy sparse format. Not normalised, not log-transformed.

required chrom ArrayLike

Chromosome per gene (1, "1" or "chr1").

required start ArrayLike

Gene start in bp per gene.

required end ArrayLike

Gene end in bp per gene.

required reference ArrayLike

Normal reference cells as a boolean mask over rows of X or integer row indices; or precomputed profiles, a float (n_genes, R) array of proportions in the gene order of X. Each cell is compared against the profile it correlates best with. Profiles are subset to the kept genes, not renormalised.

required reference_labels ArrayLike | None

Label per cell (length n_cells), read on the reference cells only. Builds one profile per label instead of pooling all reference cells into one. Not with profiles.

None params CnvParams | None

Tuning parameters, None for the defaults.

None genome Genome

Build of the default exclusion intervals (MHC and the IG/TR loci), or "none" to exclude nothing.

'hg38' n_threads int | None

Threads for this call, None for all cores.

None verbose bool

Print stage timings to stdout.

False

Returns:

Type Description CnvResult

The result; see CnvResult.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For malformed inputs.

CnvError

When the core fails, for instance with too few cells per pseudobulk.

docs.title: infer_cnv_adata
docs.text:
infer_cnv_adata(
    adata: AnnData,
    *,
    reference_key: str,
    reference_cat: str | Sequence[str],
    reference_group_key: str | None = None,
    layer: str | None = None,
    chrom_key: str = "chromosome",
    start_key: str = "start",
    end_key: str = "end",
    key_added: str = "cnv",
    params: CnvParams | None = None,
    genome: Genome = "hg38",
    n_threads: int | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> CnvResult

Run infer_cnv on an AnnData and store the result in it.

Writes, with key_added="cnv":

  • obsm["X_cnv"]: smoothed signal, cells x bins.
  • obsm["cnv_p_cnv"]: per-cell posterior of each non-neutral segment.
  • obs["cnv_p_tumour"], obs["cnv_clone"], obs["cnv_leaf"], obs["cnv_reference"] (index into reference_names).
  • uns["cnv"]: chr_pos (first bin per chromosome), bins, segments (columns of CnvResult.segments; multi_state joined with commas, nulls as -1), reference_names, params, genome.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default adata AnnData

Cells x genes. Must hold raw counts in layer (or X).

required reference_key str

obs column that labels the normal cells.

required reference_cat str | Sequence[str]

Value(s) of reference_key that are normal.

required reference_group_key str | None

obs column that splits the normal cells into one profile per value, e.g. the cell type. Can be reference_key itself. None pools them into one profile.

None layer str | None

Layer with raw counts, None for adata.X.

None chrom_key str

var column with the chromosome per gene.

'chromosome' start_key str

var column with the gene start.

'start' end_key str

var column with the gene end.

'end' key_added str

Prefix of the written slots.

'cnv' params CnvParams | None

Tuning parameters, None for the defaults.

None genome Genome

Build of the default exclusion intervals, or "none".

'hg38' n_threads int | None

Threads for this call, None for all cores.

None verbose bool

Print stage timings to stdout.

False

Returns:

Type Description CnvResult

The full CnvResult, which also carries log_odds, clone_prob and

CnvResult

genotypes.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

For a missing obs/var column or layer.

ValueError

For a reference that matches no cell, or a normal cell without a reference_group_key value.

docs.title: CnvParams dataclass
docs.text:
Tuning parameters. Defaults are numbat's (run_numbat), plus the binning, which is ours.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default window int

Running-mean window of the smoothed signal, in genes.

101 cap float

Symmetric cap on the per-gene log-ratio before smoothing.

3.0 bin_size int

Kept genes per bin of the smoothed signal.

100 init_k int

Leaf clusters cut from the cell hierarchy.

3 min_cells int

A pseudobulk needs more than this many cells.

50 t float

HMM transition probability between copy number states.

1e-05 logphi_min float

log2 fold change of a single-copy event.

0.25 min_genes int

Segments up to this many genes are smoothed away.

10 min_llr float

Segments with a lower log-likelihood ratio count as neutral.

5.0 min_overlap float

Overlap fraction that links two segments in the consensus.

0.45 max_entropy float

Segments with a higher mean p_cnv entropy are not confident.

0.5 p_multi float

Probability threshold of the multi-state test.

1.0 - 0.0001

docs.title: CnvResult dataclass
docs.text:
Output of infer_cnv.

Per-cell arrays have one row per input cell. Cells the core dropped (zero counts, or no usable reference) have used == False, NaN in float arrays and -1 in integer ones. Posterior and clone arrays are NaN for every cell when no consensus segment is non-neutral.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default used ndarray

Cells that went through the pipeline, (n_cells,) bool.

required bins ndarray

Smoothed log-ratio signal, (n_cells, n_bins) float32.

required bin_table DataFrame

One row per bin: chrom, start, end (bp), n_genes.

required leaf ndarray

Leaf cluster of the cell hierarchy per cell, -1 for none.

required segments DataFrame

One row per consensus segment. state is the HMM label, state_post the retest call (neu, amp, del, loh), p_* the retest posteriors, post_col the column in p_cnv (null for neutral segments), confident whether it passed the entropy and LLR filters.

required p_cnv ndarray

Per-cell posterior probability of each non-neutral segment, (n_cells, n_post).

required log_odds ndarray

Per-cell log-odds against neutral, (n_cells, n_post, 4); the last axis is LOG_ODDS_COLUMNS (pooled log Bayes factor, LOH, deletion, gain).

required mu ndarray

Per-cell baseline mu of the Poisson-lognormal fit.

required sigma ndarray

Per-cell baseline sigma.

required p_tumour ndarray

1 - p(normal genotype) per cell.

required clone ndarray

Most probable genotype per cell, 0 is normal.

required clone_prob ndarray

Genotype posterior, (n_cells, n_genotypes).

required genotypes list[list[tuple[int, str | None]]]

Per genotype, its events as (segment row, state); state is None unless the segment is multi-state. Genotype 0 is the empty, normal one.

required reference ndarray

Reference profile each cell correlates best with, an index into reference_names, -1 for dropped cells.

required reference_names list[str]

Name per reference profile: the label with reference_labels, otherwise its column index ("0" for pooled reference cells).

required params CnvParams

Parameters the run used.

required genome str

Exclusion intervals the run used.

required

docs.text:
LOG_ODDS_COLUMNS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "logbf",
    "loh",
    "del",

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import cnv_sc_rs as cnv

# X       scipy.sparse, cells x genes, raw counts
# chrom   per gene: 1, "1" or "chr1"
# start   per gene, bp
# end     per gene, bp
# normal  boolean mask over cells, or integer row indices

res = cnv.infer_cnv(X, chrom, start, end, reference=normal, genome="hg38")

genome picks the exclusion intervals: MHC and the IG/TR loci on "hg38" or "hg19", or "none". Match it to the build of your gene coordinates.

docs.title: Mixed references
docs.text:
Pooling T cells, myeloid cells and oligodendrocytes into one profile is a bad idea: the cell-type differences between a query cell and the pool can read as copy number change. Label the reference cells instead, and each label gets its own profile. Every cell is then compared against the profile it correlates best with, as numbat does.

# cell_type: label per cell; only the reference cells' labels are read
res = cnv.infer_cnv(X, chrom, start, end, normal, reference_labels=cell_type)

Got profiles from elsewhere, say a reference atlas? Pass them as a float (n_genes, R) array of proportions in the gene order of X, in place of the cells:

res = cnv.infer_cnv(X, chrom, start, end, profiles)

They are subset to the kept genes, not renormalised.

docs.title: Reading the result
docs.text:
res is a CnvResult. Per-cell arrays have one row per input cell; cells the pipeline dropped (zero counts) have res.used == False, NaN in float arrays and -1 in integer ones.

# consensus segments, a polars DataFrame
calls = res.segments.filter(res.segments["confident"])
calls.select("chrom", "start", "end", "n_genes", "state_post", "llr")

res.p_tumour  # per cell, 1 - p(normal genotype)
res.clone  # most probable genotype per cell, 0 is normal
res.genotypes  # per genotype: [(segment row, state), ...]
res.p_cnv  # cells x non-neutral segments, posterior of each CNV
res.bins  # cells x bins, smoothed log-ratio signal
res.bin_table  # chrom, start, end, n_genes per bin
res.reference  # reference profile per cell, index into res.reference_names

segments["post_col"] maps a segment row to its column in p_cnv and log_odds. state is the HMM label (amp1, del1, loh1, ...), state_post the retest call (neu, amp, del, loh).

If no segment comes out non-neutral, the posteriors are empty and p_tumour is NaN throughout, with a warning on the cnv_sc_rs logger.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Defaults are numbat's. Change them through CnvParams:

params = cnv.CnvParams(min_cells=30, init_k=4, min_llr=10.0)
res = cnv.infer_cnv(X, chrom, start, end, normal, params=params)

The knobs people turn first:

Parameter Default Effect min_cells 50 Smallest pseudobulk; lower it for small samples init_k 3 Leaf clusters cut from the cell hierarchy min_llr 5.0 Evidence a segment needs to count as a CNV max_entropy 0.5 Per-cell uncertainty a segment may have and stay confident

docs.title: Threads and determinism
docs.text: n_threads= caps the threads for one call; the default uses every core. The result does not depend on the thread count.

docs.title: With scanpy
docs.text: infer_cnv_adata reads raw counts and gene loci from an AnnData, runs infer_cnv and writes the result back into it. Scanpy is not a dependency; the snippets below just use it around the call.

docs.title: 1. Keep the raw counts
docs.text:
The method models UMI counts, so it needs them before any normalisation. Stash them in a layer at the start of the analysis:

import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_10x_h5("filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
adata.var_names_make_unique()
adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy()
# ... QC, normalisation, PCA, neighbours, UMAP, clustering, cell typing ...

docs.title: 2. Add gene loci to adata.var
docs.text:
infer_cnv_adata looks for var["chromosome"], var["start"] and var["end"] (change with chrom_key=, start_key=, end_key=). Genes without loci are dropped, so a partial match is fine.

From Ensembl BioMart (GRCh38, needs network), keyed on the Ensembl IDs a 10x matrix carries in var["gene_ids"]:

annot = (
    sc.queries.biomart_annotations(
        "hsapiens",
        ["ensembl_gene_id", "chromosome_name", "start_position", "end_position"],
    )
    .drop_duplicates("ensembl_gene_id")
    .set_index("ensembl_gene_id")
)

loci = annot.reindex(adata.var["gene_ids"])
adata.var["chromosome"] = loci["chromosome_name"].to_numpy()
adata.var["start"] = loci["start_position"].to_numpy()
adata.var["end"] = loci["end_position"].to_numpy()

Or from the GTF your count matrix was built with, which pins the build exactly (10x references ship it as genes/genes.gtf.gz):

import polars as pl

gtf = (
    pl.read_csv(
        "genes.gtf.gz",
        separator="\t",
        comment_prefix="#",
        has_header=False,
        quote_char=None,
        new_columns=[
            "chrom",
            "src",
            "feature",
            "start",
            "end",
            "score",
            "strand",
            "frame",
            "attr",
        ],
    )
    .filter(pl.col("feature") == "gene")
    .select(
        pl.col("attr").str.extract(r'gene_id "([^".]+)').alias("gene_id"),
        "chrom",
        "start",
        "end",
    )
    .unique("gene_id", keep="first")
)
ids = pl.DataFrame({"gene_id": adata.var["gene_ids"].to_numpy()})
loci = ids.join(gtf, on="gene_id", how="left", maintain_order="left")
adata.var["chromosome"] = loci["chrom"].to_numpy()
adata.var["start"] = loci["start"].to_numpy()
adata.var["end"] = loci["end"].to_numpy()

Chromosome labels may be 1 or chr1; both work.

docs.title: 3. Pick the reference
docs.text:
The reference should be cells you trust to be diploid: immune, endothelial or fibroblast cells from the same sample work well. Any obs column can label them:

import cnv_sc_rs as cnv

res = cnv.infer_cnv_adata(
    adata,
    reference_key="cell_type",
    reference_cat=["T cell", "B cell", "Macrophage"],
    layer="counts",
    genome="hg38",  # match the build of the loci
)

That pools all of them into one profile. With several cell types in the reference, give each its own with reference_group_key; every cell is then compared against the profile it correlates best with:

res = cnv.infer_cnv_adata(
    adata,
    reference_key="cell_type",
    reference_cat=["T cell", "B cell", "Macrophage"],
    reference_group_key="cell_type",  # or any other obs column
    layer="counts",
    genome="hg38",
)

This writes:

Slot Content obsm["X_cnv"] Smoothed log-ratio signal, cells x bins obsm["cnv_p_cnv"] Posterior of each non-neutral segment, per cell obs["cnv_p_tumour"] 1 - p(normal) per cell obs["cnv_clone"] Most probable genotype, 0 normal, -1 not used obs["cnv_leaf"] Leaf cluster of the CNV hierarchy obs["cnv_reference"] Reference profile per cell, -1 not used uns["cnv"] chr_pos, bins, segments, reference_names, params, genome

The returned CnvResult holds the same plus log_odds, clone_prob, genotypes and the segment table as a polars DataFrame.

docs.title: 4. Look at it
docs.text:
Tumour probability and genotype on the expression UMAP:

adata.obs["cnv_clone"] = adata.obs["cnv_clone"].astype("category")
sc.pl.umap(adata, color=["cell_type", "cnv_p_tumour", "cnv_clone"])

The called segments:

res.segments.filter(res.segments["confident"]).select(
    "chrom", "start", "end", "n_genes", "state_post", "llr"
)

A genome-wide heatmap of the smoothed signal, cells ordered by genotype:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

order = np.argsort(res.clone, kind="stable")
chr_pos = adata.uns["cnv"]["chr_pos"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
im = ax.imshow(
    adata.obsm["X_cnv"][order],
    aspect="auto",
    cmap="RdBu_r",
    vmin=-0.5,
    vmax=0.5,
    interpolation="nearest",
)
for pos in chr_pos.values():
    ax.axvline(pos - 0.5, color="black", lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(list(chr_pos.values()), [c.removeprefix("chr") for c in chr_pos])
ax.set_yticks([])
ax.set_ylabel("cells, by genotype")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="smoothed log ratio")

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Count matrices with float dtype are fine as long as the values are whole numbers. Normalised data is rejected.
  • min_cells (default 50) is the smallest pseudobulk. On a sample with few cells, lower it through params=cnv.CnvParams(min_cells=...).
  • Stage timings go to stdout with verbose=True. In Jupyter they appear in the terminal running the kernel, not in the notebook.
